name: Liothyronine (T3)
mechanism: Synthetic tri-iodothyronine - active form of thyroid hormone
dosing: Myxoedema coma: 5-20mcg IV/slow IV then 5-20mcg BD. Oral: rarely used, specialist only
interactions: Warfarin (↑ effect), antidiabetic drugs (may need adjustment)
monitoring: TFTs, heart rate, cardiac symptoms, clinical response
pregnancy: Continue if already on - specialist management
sideEffects: Arrhythmias, angina, tremor, restlessness, headache, hypersensitivity
pharmacokinetics: Rapid onset (hours vs weeks for T4), short half-life (2.5 days)
clinicalPearls: Rarely used - mainly myxoedema coma or specialist T3 requirement. Very expensive. Most hypothyroid patients need levothyroxine only
indication: Myxoedema coma (emergency), rarely for hypothyroidism (specialist endocrinology use only)
